name: The Ritz Carlton Tokyo
positioning: Official name The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo: a luxury hotel on the top floors of the Midtown Tower in Roppongi, with a Michelin-starred French restaurant and a spa on the 46th floor
best_for: Travelers who want a high-floor Tokyo base in Roppongi with skyline views
Food lovers who want French and Japanese dining under one roof

facts.text: The Bar is a cocktail bar and restaurant on the 45th floor with city skyline views.
Afternoon tea at The Lobby Lounge is served on Arita porcelain.
The Ritz-Carlton Spa is on the 46th floor and has skyline views.
The spa offers ESPA treatments, Bastien Gonzalez hand and foot treatments, and Shiseido Synactif treatments.
Hotel guests have complimentary access to the indoor pool, the fitness studio and the heat experience area.
The Club Lounge offers complimentary food and beverage presentations five times each day.
The hotel's restaurants and Club Lounge have views toward Shinjuku, the Imperial Palace or Mount Fuji.
Condé Nast Traveler describes the hotel as set in an actual neighborhood with many cafes and boutiques to discover during the day.

highlights.text: The hotel occupies the top nine floors of the Midtown Tower in the Roppongi District of Tokyo.
Héritage by Kei Kobayashi, the hotel's French restaurant, holds one Michelin star.
Hinokizaka, the hotel's Japanese restaurant, has separate areas for kaiseki, sushi, tempura and teppanyaki.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite features Edo-Kiriko pendant lights, ebony wood flooring and a cloud-patterned carpet.
The hotel has a patisserie, Nina, run by pastry chef Nina Métayer.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service from the airports.
Club access requires an upgraded booking, and Marriott Bonvoy Elite Status does not provide complimentary Club access.
WhataHotel notes a formal atmosphere that may not suit travelers seeking a casual stay.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo
